desc:
Choose exactly p disjoint pairs of elements from nums (no index may belong to two pairs). The cost of a choice is the largest absolute difference |a - b| over its pairs. Return the smallest cost over all possible choices. If p = 0 the cost is 0.

Example: nums = [10, 1, 2, 7, 1, 3], p = 2. Pair the two 1s (difference 0) and 2 with 3 (difference 1): the cost is 1, and no choice does better because only one pair has difference 0.
hints: Which elements are good partners for each other? Sort the array first.
Once sorted, pairs worth considering are always neighbours. If you fix the allowed difference d, you can greedily take a pair (a[i], a[i+1]) whenever it is within d and then skip both elements.
The greedy count of pairs never decreases when d grows. Binary search d in [0, max - min] for the smallest value whose greedy count reaches p.
editorial: After sorting, an optimal pairing of any size uses adjacent elements: if a < b < c < d are paired as (a, c) and (b, d) or (a, d) and (b, c), then pairing (a, b) and (c, d) has no larger difference. So with a limit d, scan left to right: if a[i+1] - a[i] ≤ d take the pair and jump two positions, otherwise move one position. Taking the leftmost possible pair never hurts, so this counts the maximum number of pairs.
The count is non-decreasing in d, so binary search the smallest d that reaches p; p = 0 returns 0 immediately. Total time O(n log n + n log(max - min)), space O(1) beyond the sorted copy.
time: O(n log n + n log R)
